_readme: Copy to config.json and edit. Every DID/handle/host below is a placeholder: point source.list_uri at your own curate list and publisher_did/owner.did at your own accounts. `python3 feedgen.py` refuses to start without config.json.
_publisher_note: The account that publishes the feed records. Every feed URI is at://<publisher_did>/app.bsky.feed.generator/<rkey> and must be published (publish_feeds.py) before clients can see it.

source._note: Candidates come from the members of this curate list: the service enumerates the list, then pulls each member's recent posts. `include_reposts` false keeps reposts out of the pool; author_feed_limit caps how far back each member is scanned.

scoring._note: Base engagement score. w_saves is structurally zero: bookmarks are private in ATProto and no public save count exists in any AppView response, so the weight always multiplies zero. It is kept visible so the term starts working if that ever changes.

owner._note: Optional featured account (the service's curator). Its posts are always candidates and get a score bonus, but they are capped at max_ratio of every feed and bypass the per-user exclusion layer, so a heavily-scrolling curator never erases their own presence. Set max_ratio to 0 to disable the feature entirely.

_blocked_note: Authors to hard-skip in every feed regardless of score. Never list owner.did here — validate with `python3 test_ranking.py feedgen.py`, which asserts it.
_topic_keywords_note: Terms that define the deployment's optional topic tilt. The service derives a per-author 'topic affinity' from the posts already stored (share of an author's posts hitting these terms), and the `topic` ranking mode weights posts by it. Empty = the topic mode is inert (its feed still works, it just carries no tilt), and `topic_seed_bonus` has no effect.
_topic_seeds_note: Optional trusted accounts for the topic tilt, as handles or DIDs. A seed is pinned to affinity 1.0 and its posts get topic_seed_bonus. Useful to bootstrap a topic before the corpus is big enough to infer it.

feeds.description: Most popular of the last 6 hours, ranked by likes and reposts.
Most popular of the last 24 hours, ranked by likes and reposts.
Most popular of the last 3 days.
Most popular of the last 7 days.
Most popular of the last 30 days.
What is rising right now: fresh posts ranked by velocity, with every fifth slot given to something being rediscovered and ranked by its recent engagement rate instead of its lifetime total.
Per-user: ranked by engagement and by what you like, never repeating what you already saw or liked, and learning from 'show less like this'.
The same pool, tilted hard toward this deployment's topic: posts are weighted by how much their author writes about the configured topic terms.

tension._note: Curator-taste tension and the per-user learning layer. `taste_weight` on each feed is how much the curator's taste shapes the shared baseline; `personal_feeds` get serve-time per-user re-ranking plus exploration slots (`explore_share` of the page is woven from curator-taste authors the requester has no signal for yet); `owner_gravity_daily` drifts a user's affinity toward curator taste (0.004/day ~ 30% convergence after 90 days for never-touched authors, while fresh interactions re-assert the user's own shape); `taste_sources` are extra accounts whose likes contribute to the taste baseline; the poll_*/likes_refresh_* budgets cap the background AppView polling that attributes likes and reposts to the requesters we served.

_hide_min_board_note: Anti-starvation floor: per-user hiding never shrinks a board below this many posts; the hidden ones come back at the tail instead. Keep it non-zero — a permanent 'seen' set with no floor once drained these feeds to a handful of posts.
_hide_seen_ttl_note: How long a post stays hidden from a user after being served in any feed of this deployment. Seen memory is shared across the deployment's feeds, so this window is what bounds its size.
